_comment: PORT campaign: IBM Spyre deeptools' SCHEDULER and BRIDGE 1, re-ported into
crates/compiler/deeptools after the first attempt was deleted whole on 2026-09-17.
⭐⭐ THE SCOPE IS THE REAL C++ TREE, NOT A VENDORED EXTRACT. A class declaration and its method
bodies are ONE unit of work here, so there is nothing to cut into an extract without splitting
exactly what must stay together. Agents read /Users/nickm/git/deeptools-src directly.
READ crustify-scheduler/AGENT-BRIEF.md IN FULL BEFORE EDITING ANYTHING. Its Rules 1 and 2 are
absolute: an agent can NEVER introduce a trait, and can NEVER make up a type.

⛔ /Users/nickm/git/deeptools is a DIFFERENT revision. Do not use it.
⛔ AND OUR OWN DOC COMMENTS ARE NOT EVIDENCE. Ten defects in the deleted port were found by reading

_comment_why_this_exists: 199,023 lines of Rust across 92 files were deleted for ~31,000 lines of working C++:
⛔ THE ALGORITHMS WERE NEVER THE PROBLEM — l3/dl_ops.rs and ddc/v1.rs held ZERO todo!s. The SHAPE
was. Both halves were made generic over traits standing in for DATA: eight in the scheduler
(Dsc2Store, Dsc2Reads, Dsc2Tree, Dsc2Stages, Dsc2Sites, Dsc2State, DdcState, DscState) and five in
the bridge (ScheduleView and Dsc among them). Every C++ member access became a trait method that
something else had to implement, and that something was schedule/stages/ — 20,494 lines with NO C++
counterpart, holding 130 todo!()s, 129 of them BARE because there was no C++ line to cite.
Five days moved that count from 131 to 130.
⛔ AND TWO VOCABULARIES FOR ONE C++ HIERARCHY IS HOW THE TREE GOT TWO HOMES: the bridge's only
`ScheduleNode` was an unrelated enum in shape_constraints.rs while the scheduler's five node structs
carried NONE of the C++ base class's 13 fields — not outerLoops_, prev_ or loop_, which are its
parent and sibling links. That is why ancestry(), producer_loops() and relevant_comps() were
unanswerable rather than unported. The scheduler and the bridge are ONE campaign so they cannot
_comment_memtrack_and_ddl_are_IN_scope: ⛔⛔ I FIRST DECLARED THESE TWO 'CLEAN, RESTORE FROM THE TAG, DO NOT RE-PORT'. THAT WAS WRONG, and
checking took one command. Restored from `scheduler-before-nuke-2026-09-17` they brought back 13
TRAIT DECLARATIONS of exactly the disease this campaign exists to remove:
ddl/conversion.rs  ScheduleReads, ScheduleWrites, DdlSite, DdlSizes, MatchSite, AllocationSite,
same shape as the deleted Dsc2Reads/Dsc2Store.
memtrack/bundle.rs GrowExPhases, ShiftExPhases, InitMemTrack — a trait PER OPERATION.
And memtrack was 4,763 Rust lines for 703 lines of C++ (6.8x), which is not what a clean port looks
⛔ THEY ALSO DO NOT STAND ALONE: the restored files reference the deleted modules FIFTY times
(ddc:: 27, l3:: 14, bridges:: 5, stages:: 3, dcg:: 1). They cannot compile without the carrier
layer, which is the proof they were never a separable clean port — they are part of the same
trait-coupled mass. So util/memtracker/mem_track.{h,cpp} (703 lines) is IN scope, and the DDL
conversion is already in scope under ddc/ (ddc/ddl/ddl_conversion.cpp — its :1065 is the
representative node-minting site, which mints a dsc2::LoopNode and registers it in loop_labels_).
⭐ WHAT REMAINS TRUE: the 32 vendored .ddl templates ARE DATA and ARE the schedule — expanding them
yields 11,218 of the reference's 14,711 nodes (76%). The templates themselves are not to be
re-derived; the C++ that PARSES and EXPANDS them is what gets ported.
_comment_acceptance: ⛔ THE GATE IS NOT `cargo test` GREEN AND IT IS NOT AN ANCHOR COUNT. The deleted port ended with
1,567 tests passing, cargo check clean, 17 of 18 units anchored — and it minted 22 nodes where the
reference mints 30 on the same program, then stopped at a carrier refusal.
⭐⭐ THE GATE IS HOW MANY NODES OUR SCHEDULER MINTS ON A REAL PROGRAM. IBM's scheduled trees hold
14,711 nodes across the 187 g0 fixture programs — transfer 3,102, compute 2,834, block 2,158, loop
is OUR INPUT (allocate nodes only, by construction) and debug/sdsc_N/sdsc.json is the reference's
SCHEDULED output at dscs_[0][<prog>].scheduleTree_. ⛔ Comparing our INPUT to their OUTPUT measures
nothing — run OUR scheduler, then compare.
Then: sdscToDataflowIR consumes that tree, dbo-opt --from-dfir bakes it, init_binary comes out.
⛔ REPORT PER UNIT, NEVER PER CAMPAIGN. A campaign cannot audit its own boundary; '1,076 units
The build gate is `cargo check -p deeptools` + `cargo test -p deeptools`; never the workspace and
never the acceptance build from an agent worktree (~6 GB of target/ each).
